title: Input-symbol interpretation of symbolic answers
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, input $x$, and width $W$, and let $\mathrm{Ans}$ assign a Boolean value to each table selector and pair of natural-number coordinates. Assume that whenever $t,a<2^W$, $\mathrm{Ans}$ agrees with the corresponding selector answer on the machine configuration reached after $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, at coordinate $a$. Then for every sign $s$ and every $t,a<2^W$, the symbolic answer for the absent-tape selector equals the input symbol of that configuration at the position offset by $(-1)^s a$ from the input head, with an out-of-range or boundary position interpreted as blank.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-tape machine with Boolean symbols and input x
A Boolean answer table indexed by selectors and two natural coordinates
For all selectors and t,a<2^W, the table agrees with the selector answer on the configuration after t steps from the initial configuration on x
